Contrarian perspectives
- Some programmes succeed when they treat transformation as operating‑model change, not as projects. Product funding, outcome KPIs, and adoption‑centred governance correlate with better results in practitioner cases; however, independent, controlled evidence is limited. ([itrevolution.com](https://itrevolution.com/articles/project-to-product-transformation-case-study-global-media-service-provider/?utm_source=openai))
- Governance isn’t inherently the problem—misapplied governance is. Assurance that tests user outcomes and operability, coupled with outcome‑based contracts, can speed learning and reduce risk. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-digital-data-and-technology-playbook/contracting-for-agile-guidance-note-html?utm_source=openai))
- The real failure rate is contested; “70% failure” lacks solid grounding. Plan with humility but avoid doom statistics to justify one-size-fits-all methods. ([thelangfordinstitute.org](https://www.thelangfordinstitute.org/articles/where-the-70-percent-change-failure-rate-came-from/?utm_source=openai))
